name: jacobi_stencil_inplace
task: This project relaxes a 2D heat plate with Jacobi iteration, split across multiple translation units: include/grid.h + src/grid.cpp (a row-major grid of doubles, a hot-plate initializer and a total-heat helper), include/heat.h + src/heat.cpp (serial and OpenMP-parallel Jacobi solvers), include/simulation.h + src/simulation.cpp (run_simulation(), built on solve_heat_parallel()), and src/main.cpp (the profiling entry point). solve_heat_parallel() in src/heat.cpp parallelizes the row loop of each sweep with '#pragma omp parallel for reduction(max : residual)', but it reads the four neighbours from and writes the new value into the same grid. Jacobi iteration requires every cell of a sweep to be computed from the values of the previous sweep; updating in place mixes old and new neighbour values (and, across threads, introduces a data race), so the result differs from solve_heat_serial(), which uses a second buffer, and run_simulation() inherits the error. Fix solve_heat_parallel() so the final grid and the returned residual are bit-for-bit identical to solve_heat_serial() for any iteration count, while keeping the cell-update loop parallelized with OpenMP (do not simply remove the pragma or serialize the loop; for example read from one buffer and write to a second one and swap them between sweeps). Do not change any function signature declared in include/grid.h, include/heat.h or include/simulation.h.
notes: build_command compiles the profiling entry point at build/app (src/main.cpp -> grid.cpp, heat.cpp, simulation.cpp). This binary must be built and then executed via run_command to drive DiscoPoP's instrumentation and produce its dynamic profiling output, including dynamic_dependencies, over the stencil loop nest in solve_heat_parallel(). test_command builds and runs a separate correctness harness at build/run_tests (from tests/test_main.cpp); it is independent of the profiling binary and should not be used as the DiscoPoP execution target. Both binaries link the same grid.cpp, heat.cpp, simulation.cpp object files, so no separate CMake/Meson/etc. configuration is required — plain 'make' is sufficient to build, run, and test.
